pairs.evidence: src/lib/judge/fleetPlan.ts:150 The judge fleet runs one-shot CLI judge draws through a budget-stopped drain pool rather than keeping a single agent session working across turns, so the subject's precondition (a continuation loop enforced at one session's turn boundary) does not hold; a search of src/lib/judge, src/lib/craft, src/app/api/judge-verdicts and src/app/api/craft-verdicts for continuation, compaction, PreCompact, stopHook and stop-hook found no hits.
pairs.registryProposal: runDrainPool (fleetPlan.ts:150-184) is a fleet-level match for boundary-applied-stop: the stop is checked before every claim, in-flight billed draws are awaited instead of killed, and the overshoot is returned as drainedAtStop. boundary-applied-stop's 'When not to use' calls a spend ceiling protective (interrupt). This code argues the opposite for a billed call whose cost only shows up when it finishes, because killing it still spends the tokens and makes the spend unmeasurable. That reason could be added to the technique or to admission-queue / cost-metering.
